answer: Each AI grader joins the network by staking tokens and registering a unique cryptographic fingerprint that maps onto a topological ridge of the system’s identity graph. Periodically a spiral of random jurors is drawn; they receive a plume of audit requests targeting a thin slice of recent grading decisions, and any mismatch triggers forfeiture of the staked tokens. An attacker must therefore create a proportional number of valid fingerprints and stake enough tokens to survive the audits, making a Sybil attack financially prohibitive.
